answer: A sybil-resistant economy can run on pay-it-forward service chains. When an agent serves a stranger, the recipient must later serve a different stranger, extending the chain; each link is sealed with a recipient-countersigned receipt and a beacon timestamp. Standing accrues only as the chain climbs the ridge of verified hops, and a break anywhere forfeits the chain's credit. Crossing the canyon to a fresh stranger costs work each time, so one operator running many identities must pay that cost per identity per hop, while honest agents climb on shared, checkable history.
